key_insight: Dex-One2Many shows that a single human demonstration can be turned into a policy that generalizes to many different initial poses, goals, and grasps. It combines demonstration guidance with exploration so the robot learns beyond simple motion copying.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of learning dexterous manipulation from only one human video without overfitting to the exact demonstrated motion. Existing imitation methods generalize poorly, while pure reinforcement learning is too hard to explore efficiently in high-dimensional manipulation tasks.
method: Uses one human demonstration as a compact prior for robot learning instead of requiring many robot demos.
Balances imitation guidance with reinforcement learning so the policy can explore while staying anchored to the demonstrated task intent.
Learns a one-to-many manipulation policy that can succeed across varied object starts, target poses, and grasps.
impact: This is useful for practitioners because it reduces the need for expensive robot data collection while improving robustness beyond exact trajectory imitation. It points toward scalable dexterous manipulation systems that can learn from minimal human input and adapt in real-world settings.
